title: Ginkgolide A alleviated liver fibrosis by modulating PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB signaling to inhibit M1 macrophage polarization and macrophage-HSC crosstalk.
authors: He, Jingxin; Zhang, Chen; Luo, Yingming; Qin, Yebi; Feng, Wanying; Yang, Jiafan; Tang, Yuqian; Jiang, Zhao; Chen, Yingxi; Cui, Hui
one_liner_zh: 研究银杏内酯A通过PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB通路抑制巨噬细胞极化缓解肝纤维化，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Liver fibrosis (LF) is a progressive pathological process driven by chronic hepatocyte injury and aberrant wound healing, culminating in excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition primarily mediated by activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). A dysregulated hepatic immune microenvironment, orchestrated in large part by macrophages, plays a critical role in driving HSCs activation. Ginkgolide A (GA), a bioactive diterpenoid lactone from Ginkgo biloba leaves, possesses potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. However, its role and underlying mechanism in LF, particularly via modulation of macrophage-HSC crosstalk, remain unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that GA inhibited LPS-induced M1 macrophage polarization and TGF-beta1-induced HSCs activation. In vivo, GA exerted potent antifibrotic effects in both NASH-associated and CCl(4)-induced liver fibrosis. Network pharmacology analysis identified the PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB signaling pathway as a key pathway targeted by GA in LF, and molecular docking and dynamics simulations further supported the interaction between GA and PI3K. Mechanistically, GA inhibited PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB signaling, and rescue experiments using a PI3K activator confirmed that this pathway is functionally required for GA-mediated suppression of M1 macrophage polarization. Collectively, GA alleviated LF by modulating PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB signaling to inhibit M1 macrophage polarization and the pathogenic macrophage-HSC interaction, highlighting its potential as an immunomodulatory therapeutic candidate for LF.
abstract_zh: 肝纤维化（LF）是一种由慢性肝细胞损伤和异常伤口愈合驱动的进行性病理过程，最终导致以活化的肝星状细胞（HSCs）为主的细胞外基质（ECM）过度沉积。由巨噬细胞在很大程度上调控的失调肝脏免疫微环境，在驱动HSCs活化中发挥关键作用。银杏内酯A（GA）是从银杏叶中提取的一种具有生物活性的二萜内酯，具有强效的抗炎和抗氧化活性。然而，其在LF中的作用及潜在机制，特别是通过调节巨噬细胞-HSC相互作用，仍不清楚。在本研究中，我们证明GA抑制了LPS诱导的M1巨噬细胞极化和TGF-β1诱导的HSCs活化。在体内，GA在NASH相关和CCl(4)诱导的肝纤维化中均表现出强效的抗纤维化作用。网络药理学分析将PI3K/AKT/NF-κB信号通路确定为GA在LF中靶向的关键通路，分子对接和动力学模拟进一步支持了GA与PI3K之间的相互作用。机制上，GA抑制了PI3K/AKT/NF-κB信号传导，使用PI3K激活剂的拯救实验证实该通路对GA介导的M1巨噬细胞极化抑制具有功能必要性。综上，GA通过调节PI3K/AKT/NF-κB信号传导抑制M1巨噬细胞极化及致病性巨噬细胞-HSC相互作用，从而缓解LF，凸显其作为LF免疫调节治疗候选药物的潜力。
